title: Minimal Polynomial = lcm of the Annihilator Polynomials of a Basis
description: Viewing Kⁿ as a K[X]-module via a matrix M, proves that the minimal polynomial of M is the least common multiple of the order (annihilator) polynomials of the vectors of any basis. At the ideal level: span{minpoly K M} is the intersection of the vector-annihilator ideals over a spanning family; the intersection of finitely many principal ideals in K[X] is generated by the lcm of their generators; hence minpoly K M = Finset.univ.lcm μ for generators μᵢ of the basis-vector annihilators.

overview.historicalContext: Fixing an n×n matrix M over a field K turns Kⁿ into a module over K[X], with X acting as M. The annihilator of a single vector v is the ideal {f : K[X] | f(M)·v = 0}; since K[X] is a PID this is generated by a single monic polynomial — the order (local minimal polynomial) of v. The parent entry cayley-hamilton-oq-01 identified the whole-space annihilator with span{minpoly K M}, and the sibling cayley-hamilton-oq-01-oq-01 developed the per-vector annihilator ideal and the cyclic case. The classical structure theory says the minimal polynomial is the lcm of the orders of any generating set; this entry formalizes that lcm characterization over a basis.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question (from cayley-hamilton-oq-01)**: Prove that the minimal polynomial of M equals the least common multiple of the annihilator (order) polynomials of the vectors of a basis.

**Resolution**: We prove (1) span{minpoly K M} = ⨅ᵢ vecAnnIdeal M (vᵢ) for any spanning family v; (2) ⨅ᵢ span{aᵢ} = span{Finset.univ.lcm a} in K[X]; (3) combining these over a basis b with generators μᵢ of vecAnnIdeal M (bᵢ): span{minpoly K M} = span{Finset.univ.lcm μ}; and (4) the literal polynomial identity minpoly K M = Finset.univ.lcm μ, together with the existence of monic such generators.
overview.text: A 187-line, axiom-free development (8 theorems, 0 definitions) over the K[X]-module Module.AEval' M.mulVecLin from the sibling entry cayley-hamilton-oq-01-oq-01. The headline minpoly_span_eq_iInf_vecAnnIdeal shows that for any family v whose range spans Kⁿ, the minimal-polynomial ideal is the intersection of the vector annihilators: the ≤ direction is the reused minpoly_ideal_le_vecAnnIdeal, and the ≥ direction uses that a polynomial killing every spanning vector kills the whole endomorphism (LinearMap.ext_on_range), so minpoly ∣ it (minpoly.dvd). The bridge iInf_span_singleton_eq_lcm turns the intersection of finitely many principal ideals into the ideal of the lcm via Finset.lcm_dvd_iff. minpoly_span_eq_lcm_of_generators composes the two over a basis. The literal identity minpoly_eq_lcm follows because span{minpoly} = span{lcm} gives Associated, and both polynomials are monic (minpoly by Cayley-Hamilton integrality; Finset.lcm is normalized, hence monic when nonzero), so eq_of_monic_of_associated yields equality — notably with no monicity hypothesis on the generators. exists_monic_generators produces the monic order polynomials via the PID generator and normalize, and exists_minpoly_eq_lcm packages the headline.
overview.proofStrategy: The crux is the ≥ inclusion of minpoly_span_eq_iInf_vecAnnIdeal. Given f in every vector annihilator, extract aeval M.mulVecLin f (vᵢ) = 0 from the AEval' scalar action; since the vᵢ span, LinearMap.ext_on_range gives aeval M.mulVecLin f = 0; then minpoly.dvd plus minpoly K M = minpoly K M.mulVecLin yields minpoly K M ∣ f. The lcm bridge is a membership calculation: x ∈ ⨅ᵢ span{aᵢ} ↔ ∀ i, aᵢ ∣ x ↔ lcm ∣ x ↔ x ∈ span{lcm} (Finset.lcm_dvd_iff). For the literal identity, Ideal.span_singleton_eq_span_singleton converts the span equality to Associated; monicity of the lcm comes from monic_normalize together with Finset.normalize_lcm (the lcm is its own normalization), and nonvanishing of the lcm follows since minpoly ≠ 0; eq_of_monic_of_associated closes it.
keyInsights: The minimal polynomial generates the intersection of the annihilator ideals of any spanning set — the ideal-theoretic form of 'minpoly = lcm of the orders of the basis vectors'.
A polynomial kills the endomorphism f(M) iff it kills a spanning family, so the global annihilator is exactly the meet of the local (per-vector) annihilators.
In K[X] the intersection of principal ideals is the lcm ideal (Finset.lcm_dvd_iff), turning the meet of orders directly into a least common multiple.

The polynomial identity minpoly K M = Finset.univ.lcm μ needs NO monicity assumption on the generators μᵢ: a Finset.lcm is automatically normalized (monic), and minpoly is monic, so being associated forces equality.
Monicity of the minimal polynomial — needed nowhere explicitly except to pin the lcm down to an equality — comes for free from Cayley-Hamilton via integrality of M.

sections.title: Overview: minpoly as the lcm of Basis-Vector Orders
sections.summary: Frames the result: the minimal polynomial of a matrix M is the lcm of the order (annihilator) polynomials of the vectors of any basis of Kⁿ. Sets up Kⁿ as a K[X]-module via M (parent's vecAnnIdeal framework) and the two forms — an ideal identity and a literal polynomial equality minpoly K M = Finset.univ.lcm μ.
sections.mathContext: $\minpoly_K M = \operatorname{lcm}_i \mu_i$, where $\mu_i$ generates the annihilator ideal of basis vector $b_i$.

sections.title: Helpers: minpoly of mulVecLin and Integrality
sections.summary: minpoly_mulVecLin_eq (minpoly K M = minpoly K M.mulVecLin, via Matrix.minpoly_toLin') and isIntegral_matrix (every matrix over a field is integral — Cayley–Hamilton, witnessed by the monic charpoly). These license the minpoly-divides and monic arguments below.
sections.mathContext: $\minpoly_K M = \minpoly_K M_{\mathrm{mulVecLin}}$; $M$ integral via $\chi_M$ monic with $\chi_M(M)=0$.

sections.title: Part I — minpoly Ideal = Intersection of Vector Annihilators
sections.summary: minpoly_span_eq_iInf_vecAnnIdeal: for any spanning family v, span{minpoly K M} = ⨅ᵢ vecAnnIdeal M (vᵢ). One inclusion is that minpoly kills every vector; the converse is that a polynomial killing a spanning family kills M as an endomorphism (LinearMap.ext_on_range), so minpoly divides it.
sections.mathContext: $\langle\minpoly_K M\rangle = \bigcap_i \operatorname{Ann}(v_i)$ for any family $v$ with $\operatorname{span}\{v_i\} = K^n$.

sections.title: Part II — Intersection of Principal Ideals = lcm
sections.summary: iInf_span_singleton_eq_lcm: in the PID K[X], ⨅ᵢ span{aᵢ} = span{Finset.univ.lcm a}, unfolded directly from Finset.lcm_dvd_iff. The purely ideal-theoretic bridge that turns the intersection of Part I into an lcm.

sections.title: Part III — minpoly = lcm of Basis Order Polynomials
sections.summary: Combines Parts I & II. minpoly_span_eq_lcm_of_generators gives the ideal form span{minpoly} = span{lcm μ}. exists_monic_generators produces monic order polynomials (each annihilator is principal in the PID; normalize the generator). minpoly_eq_lcm upgrades associated-ideals to a literal equality using monicity of both minpoly and the normalized Finset.lcm.
sections.mathContext: $\minpoly_K M = \operatorname{Finset.univ.lcm}\ \mu$ — associated ideals + both sides monic $\Rightarrow$ equal.

sections.title: Headline: Existence of a Monic lcm Decomposition
sections.summary: exists_minpoly_eq_lcm bundles it: for any basis b there exist monic order polynomials μᵢ generating the annihilator ideals with minpoly K M = Finset.univ.lcm μ — the clean statement of the minimal polynomial as an lcm of basis-vector orders.

conclusion.summary: Viewing Kⁿ as a K[X]-module via M, the minimal polynomial of M is the least common multiple of the order polynomials of the vectors of any basis. Proved in three layers: span{minpoly K M} equals the intersection of the vector-annihilator ideals over a spanning family; the intersection of finitely many principal ideals in K[X] is generated by the lcm of the generators; and the resulting span equality upgrades to the literal polynomial identity minpoly K M = Finset.univ.lcm μ because both sides are monic and associated. Fully verified, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.
conclusion.implications: This gives the lcm characterization of the minimal polynomial in terms of a basis, completing the per-vector annihilator theory of cayley-hamilton-oq-01-oq-01 to the whole space. It is the computational route to the minimal polynomial used in the rational-canonical-form and invariant-factor algorithms, where one assembles minpoly from the orders of a generating set.
openQuestions: Refine the lcm to the full invariant-factor chain d₁ | ... | dₖ = minpoly by intersecting/decomposing the per-vector orders.
Show the lcm is attained by a single vector (existence of a vector whose order equals the minimal polynomial), the cyclic-vector existence theorem in the non-derogatory case.
Replace the basis by an arbitrary finite generating set and relate the order multiset to the elementary divisors of M.
